conflicts.description: The Office of Final Copies wants the audit to endorse its transcript before the next tide exposes the original. The Bellkeepers can delay the audit by changing the signal sequence, but doing so would reveal who ordered the bridge lights dark during the archivist's last crossing.
conflicts.name: The Original and the Copy

description: Tidemark is a rain-lashed city balanced on pilings above a drowned archive. Its two surviving districts are joined by a skybridge whose glass floor makes every crossing a public performance. In this sarcastic thriller, a civic demonstration meant to prove the city’s records are infallible becomes a hunt for the person who edited a death into a resignation. The city has a tidy answer for every question, usually printed in triplicate; the trouble is that the tide keeps returning the originals.

factions.description: Registry clerks who certify births, deaths, and civic truths. They insist every discrepancy is a filing error and treat public confidence as a more delicate document than any original.
factions.name: The Office of Final Copies

factions.description: Signal tenders who maintain the pressure bells and control the lantern sequence across the districts. Their old duty is to warn of dangerous tides; their newer habit is to decide which warnings count.
factions.name: The Bellkeepers

history.description: A storm drowned the old records beneath Morrow Quay. The Office of Final Copies replaced them with certified transcripts, then quietly declared the transcripts more reliable than memory.
history.name: The Archive Flood

history.description: The Bellkeepers opened the glass crossing between Crown Spindle and the quay, promising that a city where everyone could see everyone else would have fewer secrets. The promise became a slogan before the first maintenance bill arrived.
history.name: The Span of Good Faith

history.description: On the eve of a public audit, an archivist's death record was replaced by a resignation dated one day later. The registry says the matter is settled; the tide has begun leaving salt on the supposedly untouched original.
history.name: The Resignation That Wasn't

locations.description: A crowded harbor district of salt-stained offices, ferry stairs, and warehouses perched above the black water. The municipal registry occupies an old customs house where clerks can hear the tide knock beneath the floor whenever a record is altered.
locations.name: Morrow Quay

locations.description: A narrow tower district built around the city’s pressure bells and signal lanterns. Its public skybridge connects the tower to Morrow Quay; translucent panels reveal anyone crossing, unless the bells ring and the whole span shivers with reflected light.
locations.name: Crown Spindle

name: The Tidemark Ledger

rules.statement: The rising tide leaves a fresh salt line on every surface touched by seawater, including sealed paper and locked doors.
A pressure bell's final echo lasts exactly seven breaths, and no lantern signal can be trusted while it sounds.
A civic record becomes legally binding only when its maker and one witness sign the same page in daylight.
